fields.title: Earlier, Not Before Release
fields.keyTakeaway: Four discovery questions and triage across six criteria filter out most features, and full reviews are run for the rest—before design, not before release.
fields.sections/0/blocks/0/text: Why is a security review before release a bad idea?
fields.sections/1/blocks/0/text: A review at the end finds design flaws when everything is already built. The choice becomes between reworking the feature or releasing with a known problem. Both options are expensive, and both stem from the timing of the review rather than work quality.
fields.sections/2/blocks/0/text: Three points where security can get involved:
fields.sections/2/blocks/1/text: **In discovery.** Before deciding what to build. Cheap, influences solution choice. **In design.** Threat modeling, discussed above. Cheap, influences architecture. **Before release.** Expensive, influences only the date.
fields.sections/2/blocks/2/text: The right approach is the first two; the third acts as a verification check, not as the initial meeting.
fields.sections/2/blocks/4/text: *What data does the feature touch?* Do new personal data types appear. *Does the access model change?* *Are there new data recipients?* *Are there compliance obligations?* Localization, consents, retention periods.
fields.sections/2/blocks/5/text: Four questions, five minutes, and they determine whether a full review is needed.
fields.sections/2/blocks/6/text: **Triage**—not every feature requires a full review. Criteria that trigger one:
fields.sections/2/blocks/7/text: *New personal data.* *New external recipient.* *Changes to access rights.* *Features handling money.* *Communication between users.* *Automated decisions about people.*
fields.sections/2/blocks/8/text: Everything else passes without a review. This is what keeps the process functional: reviewing everything stops people from doing reviews at all.
fields.sections/2/blocks/9/text: **[[security-review-2|Review]] by a specialist**—for features from the list. Not sign-off, but participation: the specialist joins during design rather than reading the outcome.
fields.sections/3/blocks/0/text: The four questions are built into the discovery template. Filled out by the PM in five minutes.
fields.sections/3/blocks/1/text: Triage: out of 34 features over six months, a full review was needed for 7. The rest passed through the four questions.
fields.sections/3/blocks/2/text: Process change yielded measurable results: previously, two features a year hit a blocker before release with an average delay of three weeks. Afterward—zero.
fields.sections/3/blocks/3/text: A telling case: the "invite a friend and get a bonus" feature triggered two criteria during discovery—inter-user communication and money. The review found an abuse scheme involving fake accounts and changed the mechanics prior to implementation: the bonus is granted after the invited user's first order rather than after registration.
fields.sections/3/blocks/4/text: The security specialist participates in design every two weeks on a schedule—not on demand, which removes the friction of reaching out.
fields.sections/4/blocks/0/text: The process works with a small number of features requiring review. With growth, you need either a dedicated person or a stricter triage.
fields.sections/5/blocks/0/text: Four questions in discovery and triage by six criteria filter out most features, and a full review is conducted for the remaining ones — before design, not before release.
